## Operational delivery sequence (2026-10-04) {#operational-delivery}

*Working implementation sequence, not a claim of additional server acceptance.*
[D-025](../decisions.qmd#d-025) separates preserved execution, recoverable
provenance, and identical stochastic replay. The replay counterexample remains
an owner-reviewed follow-up, not a prerequisite for every operator deliverable.

1. **Actual stage-1 predecessor handoff — passed.** The diagnostic
   [analyses `d23deca5`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/commit/d23deca51b33f18bcbf3c726bf7b9264141caab0)
   copies `calib.10.1.stage0` and `calib.10.1.stage1` into isolated test codes with
   two iterations and no thinning. Likelihoods, sampled parameter sets, aliases,
   solver settings, managers, and predecessor weighting stay unchanged.
   Completed-state inspection requires the actual MSM diagnosis likelihood term,
   finite stored samples/likelihoods/priors, and exact copying of model parameters
   from the predecessor summary. Output lineage and simset inspection follow,
   then a repeated pipeline must verify and skip both completed stages. The
   [hosted run](https://github.com/ncsizemore/jheem-containers/actions/runs/37203984715)
   passed with [container source `979c0093`](https://github.com/ncsizemore/jheem-containers/commit/979c00930ddcd8523d3503a5d6e5c18a44498024).
   Downloaded reports verified all 173 transferred parameters exactly, stage 0's
   88 and stage 1's 87 sampled variables, six and twelve registered likelihood
   terms respectively, and two completed simulations per stage. Stored total
   likelihoods, priors, parameters, and selected outcome totals were finite;
   predecessor/output digests and verify/skip on repetition passed. Diagnostics
   and the [short results report](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/0de5aa3e65bd057ac92aa6f00dee57f03c092828/applications/SHIELD/tests/STAGE1-HANDOFF.md)
   landed on analyses master `0de5aa3e` and
   [container main `6dd6d3a0`](https://github.com/ncsizemore/jheem-containers/commit/6dd6d3a0a5bc54f8a1b4eb2033f1f82f2e22bc05).
   This test is neither a realistic-duration calibration nor convergence evidence.
2. **Current-runtime operator trial.** Retain a tested runtime separately from
   the installed October 1 image. Select committed source, intended manager
   releases, a representative single-chain stage, and a fresh output root with
   the model operators. Exercise the existing guide from another account;
   collect setup/start/status/logging feedback, elapsed time and peak memory,
   completed output/lineage checks, and the preserved source/input/runtime
   identities. Keep active scientific runs and their history unchanged.
   Hosted preparation does not require server NAS access; live server acceptance
   still requires the actual shared-storage and account checks.
3. **Full-calibration support.** Stage 3 currently has four chains, while the
   recorded launcher deliberately refuses more than one. Specify per-chain
   execution, completion/assembly, restart behavior, and writer coordination
   before implementing a multi-chain adapter. A native handoff is an alternative
   only after its inputs, outputs, and environment are explicitly verified.
   Do not describe single-chain acceptance as full-workflow readiness.
4. **Artifact-led provenance recovery.** Reconcile adjacent receipts and
   digest-led lookup with the current recorded run tree. Add automatic,
   retryable retention and demonstrate recovery from a copied simset without
   knowledge of its original directory. Metadata and source retention, large
   scientific artifacts, manager bytes, and runtime preservation are distinct
   obligations; a recorded identifier is not proof that its bytes remain
   recoverable. See the [provenance design](reproducibility.qmd#artifact-led-discovery).

Image retention/publication, server installation, and a scientific run are
separate steps. Neither a hosted check nor a new image changes the installed
runtime automatically. The handoff run tested image
`sha256:4eae3c47f8a2a1920aacd84d5ac463529abc3f2bf7581b63ea255c16899764b6`
with September 9 syphilis/August 26 census inputs, seed 0, one BLAS thread, and
no execution-time network. It uploaded reports, not an installable image, and
did not change the server installation. Hosted reports expire after 14 days;
retaining a deployable runtime remains a separate step. The checkpoint/RNG
proposal must retain the measured restart limitation until a reviewed correction
passes the replay check.

## SHIELD reference-workflow checkpoint (2026-09-17)

A failed SHIELD stage-3 calibration was initially presented as a shared-storage
interruption because the launcher caught any `run.calibration()` error, replaced
its message with a write-interruption explanation, and retried. Direct checks of
the output roots and lower-level file operations did not reproduce a storage
failure. The same calibration then failed against a local output root, and the
failure was traced to a likelihood term with a zero denominator. This incident
joins three reproducibility questions that were previously being treated
separately: whether the real error remains observable, whether the scientific
inputs and environment can be reconstructed, and whether an interrupted
calibration follows the same stochastic path when resumed.

Current `jheem_analyses` `master` changes the future-growth ratio denominator from
`start` to `start + 1` in
[`55bd55c6`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/commit/55bd55c6975c09063c8c62828bf52f6a9da31eb3).
That makes the immediate division finite but also defines scientific behavior for
zero and small baselines. Engineering work may reproduce the edge cases, preserve
the original error, and add characterization or non-finite-likelihood checks. A
different formula, pseudocount, exclusion rule, or expected value should not be
selected through an infrastructure change; the intended behavior needs explicit
scientific review before it becomes a regression assertion.

The sampler currently lacks a coherent explicit-seed contract. At
[`bayesian.simulations@4e0d13e`](https://github.com/tfojo1/bayesian.simulations/commit/4e0d13e85857396bb0e6e2ac1d244775b2145f75):

- `create.mcmc.cache(seed = ...)` validates `seed` but does not pass it to
  `do.create.cache()`, whose signature requires it;
- `do.create.chain.cache.controls(..., seed)` accepts the value but generates
  per-chunk seeds with `runif()` from ambient R state rather than from that
  argument; and
- `jheem2::set.up.calibration()` exposes no seed argument, so current application
  setup relies on prior global RNG state.

Per-chunk seed storage was introduced in
[`b170ce7`](https://github.com/tfojo1/bayesian.simulations/commit/b170ce7e5c265fa7540a2847a8bc894fa797dd2c),
after the `34840866` revision currently installed by the container base lock.
Consequently, the existing container canary proves that a partial cache can be
continued to its remaining chunk; it does not prove that an explicit seed controls
the schedule, that interrupted and uninterrupted traces are equal, or that the
same request is reproducible across the team's servers.

Two review branches establish useful but incomplete evidence:

- [`jheem_analyses@accd7b64`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/commit/accd7b64dd0ab1f38f5ccad993a643c3c7544de2)
  stages automatic provenance, immutable source declarations, read-only manager
  caches, truthful failure/resume behavior, and a bounded SHIELD canary. It split
  from `master` at `ea111ea3` and must be reconciled with later application work,
  including the likelihood change, before it can be proposed for ordinary use.
- [`jheem-containers@262c733`](https://github.com/ncsizemore/jheem-containers/commit/262c733d5c71ec4aa480dde4131880002105dc31)
  builds a pinned SHIELD image and has completed a real-engine preflight plus a
  forced-interruption/resume canary in CI. The image still pins the older sampler,
  the canary is a tiny stage-0 path rather than the failing stage-3 path, and no
  uninterrupted-versus-resumed or cross-server equality comparison is made.

These are validation assets, not yet evidence that SHIELD calibration is
reproducible. The 2026-09-17 sequence prioritized a small, executable sampler
seed demonstration and focused correction before SHIELD branch reconciliation.
The narrower container-pilot sequence is updated below; it does not remove the
need to test the sampler behavior behind a deterministic-replay claim. The
[October 3 refinement](#repeatability-plan) distinguishes testing the current
workflow from correcting the explicit seed argument.

## SHIELD container-pilot update (2026-09-22)

The team is evaluating containerization of SHIELD as an operational deliverable.
That question is narrower than whether an earlier calibration can be reproduced
exactly. The [existing container spike](https://github.com/ncsizemore/jheem-containers/blob/262c733d5c71ec4aa480dde4131880002105dc31/workloads/shield/README.md)
builds a pinned image and exercises a small real-engine calibration through a
forced interruption and checkpoint continuation in hosted CI. It has not yet
run on a team server, completed production-sized simset assembly there, or
compared uninterrupted and resumed scientific traces.

The spike pins `jheem_analyses@accd7b64`, while the verified active branch is
`master@16eff985`, 71 commits ahead of the common base with the staged
`codex/shield-source-readiness` branch. The active SHIELD tree now has a
[three-tier model-test workflow](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/16eff985372fd65be46871bf164acb6eff14beb3/.github/workflows/test-shield.yml)
and a [calibration launcher](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/16eff985372fd65be46871bf164acb6eff14beb3/applications/SHIELD/shield_calib_setup_and_run.R)
that prints the original error and stops on many non-storage failures. Those
changes supersede parts of the staged branch, but ordinary setup still defaults
to clearing state and uses a fixed `set.seed(0)` before calibration. The
[source bootstrap](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/16eff985372fd65be46871bf164acb6eff14beb3/applications/SHIELD/shield_source_code.R)
still requires a sibling `jheem2` checkout on `dev` in source mode, and can pull
when interactive. A recorded container run needs an explicit, non-mutating
source and run-mode contract; the older branch supplies candidate pieces, not a
merge-ready replacement for the current application.

The new test workflow is useful characterization, not yet a dependable green
gate: the [2026-09-22 run](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/actions/runs/35762822719)
failed in the static tier and skipped the later tiers. Its
[README](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/16eff985372fd65be46871bf164acb6eff14beb3/applications/SHIELD/tests/README.md)
says some tests intentionally fail to preserve open code-review findings. At
least one static test asserts that the `+1` growth-penalty denominator should be
removed and suggests alternatives; because that is a scientific formula choice,
it should be resolved by the scientific owners, not silently changed as
container-readiness work.

A clean local checkout of the same pinned analyses commit reproduced 11 static
assertion failures and 3 static skips. Running the unit-file subset independently
returned 6 assertion failures, 4 errors, and 4 skips; missing test-bootstrap
inputs account for some of those errors and skips, so these counts are not a
model-defect count. The workflow chains static → unit → integration with `needs`,
which means a persistently red static tier prevents the model tier from running.
Conversely, the
[test runner](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/16eff985372fd65be46871bf164acb6eff14beb3/applications/SHIELD/tests/run_tests.R#L94-L114)
exits nonzero only for failed assertions or errors: if required bootstrap stages
are unavailable and tests only skip, a tier can appear green without exercising
its intended model path. Before using this workflow as a container acceptance
gate, separate open diagnostic findings from must-pass checks and make missing
required integration prerequisites fail explicitly. Text matching for a local
`set.seed()` call and the growth-penalty formula test are examples that need a
contract-level or domain-reviewed assertion rather than an automatic code edit.

A bounded pilot should therefore establish, in order: a pinned image built
against current SHIELD source; identified manager assets and source revisions;
non-destructive fresh/resume behavior; successful real-engine preflight and a
small checkpoint continuation; then a retained run on a team server that checks
mounts, file ownership, error logs, runtime, and output inspection. Full assembly
and repeated-run comparisons are separate acceptance steps. The sampler seed
finding remains recorded and should be tested before claiming deterministic
replay or equivalent results across servers.

## Recorded-run source checkpoint (2026-09-23)

[`jheem_analyses@5b377e8`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/commit/5b377e8)
is on the isolated
[`codex/shield-recorded-contract` branch](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/tree/codex/shield-recorded-contract),
not `master`. It adds an opt-in `SHIELD_RECORDED_RUN=true` route through the
current source bootstrap and calibration launcher. That route requires declared
source commit identities, immutable dated manager releases, verified offline
manager assets, separate input and output roots, and an explicit seed. Fresh
mode refuses existing calibration state; resume requires a matching input
receipt and readable checkpoint/progress before MCMC. A focused cache change
allows verified offline assets to load from a read-only cache without a writer
lock. The default ordinary route remains selected without the opt-in flag.
The branch changes no likelihood formula or model parameter. Its
[pilot contract and caveats](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/5b377e8/applications/SHIELD/RECORDED-RUN-PILOT.md)
remain review material, not supported production instructions.

This branch addresses the **prepared-runtime and input-identity** portion of
the broader [run-record contract](reproducibility.qmd#proposed-target-contract).
Its local `inputs.json` is not the staged automatic attempt history, an
output-linked simset receipt, or a durable archive. The container pilot should
prove that this narrow route can execute and continue safely; it must not make
the separate provenance and sampler work appear complete. A supported team
workflow should eventually supply the technical declarations behind the
existing calibration command rather than require operators to manage another
set of identifiers by hand.

Focused runtime and cache tests passed locally; the existing SHIELD static
suite still had 12 diagnostic failures and lacked local bootstrap data for its
full path. The current modular launcher is deliberately rejected in recorded
mode because it clears calibration state. The older container canary calls
that modular launcher and expects an older runtime interface and stage-0
fixture, so merely changing its analyses commit would neither run nor validate
this branch. The next gate is to reconcile the container preflight and canary
with the current recorded entrypoint, run a must-pass hosted smoke, and only
then attempt a retained team-server pilot. No deterministic-replay or
production-calibration claim follows from the source branch alone.

## Container canary and shield2 pilot (2026-09-29)

The recorded-run branch was rebased onto current `master`. Two source changes
followed. The recorded state check had rebuilt the calibration directory as
`mcmc_runs/<version>/<location>/<code>`, but `jheem2@ccb1f9b` reorders it to
`<version>/<code>/<location>`, so `resume` would have looked in the wrong
place; the check now asks jheem2 for the directory once jheem2 is loaded.
And a two-iteration `container.smoke.stage0` calibration (the real SHIELD model
and stage-0 likelihood, two parameters) is registered only when a recorded run
sets `SHIELD_ENABLE_CONTAINER_SMOKE=true`.

The container build in `jheem-containers` PR #24 was pointed at that source.
Its hosted CI now builds the recorded image, runs preflight (declared source
revisions, immutable manager releases, verified manager digests), starts a
fresh calibration, kills it once the first checkpoint is durable, and resumes
it in a separate process until the second checkpoint is durable, checking
that the first was not rewritten. It deliberately stops there. A 2-iteration
run peaks above the 16 GB hosted runner's memory while building the MCMC
summary (the kernel killed R at 15.5 GB resident), so summary and assembly are
server tests. Two test defects surfaced and were fixed: a digest comparison
that failed on an attribute, and a checkpoint check that required the control
file to be strictly newer than the chunk. Kernel timestamps are coarse, so the
control saved right after a chunk can share its timestamp.

The image CI tested (exported as an artifact, image ID `214b9677…`) was loaded
into rootless Podman on shield2 under an administrator's account:

| Run | Local-disk state | NAS state |
|---|---|---|
| Canary calibration, uninterrupted through summary and assembly | passed, 342 s | passed, 368 s |
| Kill after the first checkpoint, resume to the second | passed | passed |
| Memory: loading / sampling / summary and assembly | about 5.9 / 10.3 / 28 GB | about 5.9 / 10.3 / 28.5 GB |

Chunk files are about 265 MB each and take about 54 s to write; the global
control is about 154 MB. Writing a chunk takes longer than a sampling iteration
at this size. The simulation set is 270 MB. The stage-0 run below shows these
sizes, and the summary and assembly memory, were inflated by the image's
package installation, since fixed.

Server prerequisites observed on the RHEL 9 hosts, recorded in the server
administration repository:

- Podman is installed and Docker is not. Rootless runs use `--userns=keep-id`
  so outputs keep the user as owner; local bind mounts need an SELinux relabel.
- A rootless container is stopped about 10 seconds after its user's last login
  session ends unless lingering is enabled for that user
  (`loginctl enable-linger`). A pilot container was lost this way before
  lingering was enabled.
- Containers reach the CIFS-mounted NAS only with the `virt_use_samba` SELinux
  boolean enabled on the host, and write to it only when the container keeps
  the user's `jheem` group (`--group-add keep-groups`); without it, writes are
  refused. Both prerequisites were enabled for this pilot on shield2 only.

## Realistic stage on shield2 (2026-09-30)

`calib.9.28.stage0` for C.12580 (15,000 iterations, 30 chunks) ran in the same
image on shield2 with NAS state, one BLAS thread, and the ordinary launcher's
checkpoint settings, alongside the team's completed native run of the same
stage and location on shield1:

| | Container, shield2 | Native, shield1 |
|---|---|---|
| Result | exit 0; summary and 300-simulation set written | complete |
| Time per 500-iteration chunk | median 27.6 min (25.9–29.4) | median 29.9 min (28.8–30.9), 10 locations sharing the server |
| Sampling | 13 h 46 min at about 10.5 GB | about 15 h |
| Summary and assembly | about 12 min, peak 35.4 GB | not measured |
| Chunk file | about 305 MB | about 44 MB |
| Simulation set | 1.54 GB | 1.28 GB |

Runtime and stability are comparable. The image's analyses revision is
slightly newer than the one the native run started from, so likelihood values
are not compared.

The chunk difference was not in the number of simulations. In the container's
first chunk, the first stored simulation serialized to about 5.6 GB against
about 20 MB natively. The cause was the image installing the team packages
with kept source references. Each jheem2 R6 object stored in a simulation
(specification, solver, and run metadata) has methods whose source reference
points at the package source file, and that file's text was an unforced lazy-load
promise; saving it serialized about 2.8 GB of the package's lazy-load state per
object. Native runs source jheem2 under `Rscript`, which keeps no source
references. R's default package install doesn't keep them either.

The image now installs `distributions`, `bayesian.simulations`, `locations`, and
jheem2 with `R CMD INSTALL --without-keep.source`, fails its build if any of
them keeps source references, and pins `bayesian.simulations` and
`distributions` to the commits the team servers run (the base image had carried
an older `bayesian.simulations` without its July and August 2025 fixes). The
hosted canary now fails if its first chunk exceeds 100 MB. The same canary on
shield2 with NAS state (`jheem-containers@93bf24e`):

| | Before the fix | After the fix |
|---|---|---|
| Elapsed | 368 s | 101 s |
| Peak memory (summary and assembly) | 28.5 GB | 11.1 GB |
| Checkpoint chunk | 266 MB | 5.4 MB |
| Simulation set (2 simulations) | 270 MB | 9.6 MB |

The earlier 28 GB and 35 GB peaks therefore described the image, not SHIELD. A
full stage has not been rerun with the fixed image.

## Integration checkpoint and next sequence (2026-10-01)

The September 30 implementation adds input/output lineage, per-attempt records,
and sequential single-chain stages
([analyses `373faf27`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/commit/373faf2775f584093ac16c17ce18432959c609d9),
[containers `ad92324`](https://github.com/ncsizemore/jheem-containers/commit/ad92324f7d742d2059a31aac65a9b51e1d23c528)).
The [hosted canary](https://github.com/ncsizemore/jheem-containers/actions/runs/36776425076)
now completes summary and assembly, checks the records, and runs a two-stage
pipeline. The operator wrapper and runbook are in the container repository.
This newer path has not yet been exercised by another operator on a team server.

A negative check found a boundary defect: deleting the summary
and simulation-set files while retaining `outputs.json` still lets the pipeline
report all stages complete. The preceding-stage resolver hashes the record but
does not verify the files it describes. Completion and lineage checks therefore
needed to verify record identity and referenced output sizes and digests before
reusing a stage. A successful ordinary canary did not cover that failure mode.

That defect is now fixed in
[`jheem_analyses@06505412`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/commit/06505412ff4ad870ba0263361b791ba5d53737de),
integrated into `master` through
[`3f463e2a`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/commit/3f463e2ab274e4d5e24decdf82f294a91b628857).
The matching container implementation was integrated into `main` through
[`4b9f83db`](https://github.com/ncsizemore/jheem-containers/commit/4b9f83dbab3f784aa177947e2c27925d784eae10).
The source branch includes current application changes and verified latest-loader
integration; this increment changes no likelihood formula or sampler behavior.

[Run 36815091235](https://github.com/ncsizemore/jheem-containers/actions/runs/36815091235)
passed the offline runtime/cache tests, real-engine interruption/resume,
summary and assembly, and a two-stage pipeline. Missing simsets, same-size
modified simsets, and a changed requested seed were each rejected. Restoring
the original files and inputs allowed verified reuse. Focused tests also cover
stale preceding-stage records and interrupted setup without a checkpoint.
The ordinary SHIELD static suite still fails on existing findings and skips
later tiers; these operational checks do not resolve its scientific assertions.

The exact tested image is retained in the non-latest
[`shield-pilot-2026.10.01-r36815091235` prerelease](https://github.com/ncsizemore/jheem-containers/releases/tag/shield-pilot-2026.10.01-r36815091235),
beyond the seven-day Actions artifact lifetime. The release contains the image
archive and `IMAGE.txt` with its identity and source revisions. Its published
archive SHA-256 matches the tested export:
`01e344d5948945851f397a41e2ec24b5f77878e2335b5d8960eb5a5a3a81e60c`.
This retains the runtime, not scientific outputs or their run records; canary
logs and records remain in their temporary CI artifact.

### Operator handoff (2026-10-01)

The [operator guide](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/72922ef9f54e72ef57d9a31d9368e687f77aff7b/applications/SHIELD/CONTAINER-PILOT.md)
now lives beside SHIELD in `jheem_analyses`, linked from its server guide and
recorded-runtime reference. Operators use an installed wrapper; they need no
container-repository checkout. The
[administrator runbook](https://github.com/ncsizemore/jheem-containers/blob/717875b7d8fbb2f69ce52b5f519fd3c819e22c56/workloads/shield/RUNBOOK.md)
stays in `jheem-containers` and separates installation/account verification from
the subsequent independent operator exercise. Default-branch publication is not
evidence that the intended server accounts are ready.

This handoff retains the tested image's analyses snapshot `06505412`. Newer
master changes include STI-screening modifier behavior
([`3f9e2019`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/commit/3f9e2019068a8d9e2cb6eb94426fdd947a4d9756))
and widening `TRATE_DELTA` from 1.5 to 3
([`207672f2`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/commit/207672f2c1fa9dbf588a9fbafa4307ab8e9dc5ce)); the image does not include
them. Trying its operational mechanics is separate from selecting code and
inputs for a scientific calibration. The guide explicitly says not to delay
ordinary full calibrations: multi-chain stage 3 and native handoff remain
unsupported.

The wrapper now rejects a fresh start when only a previous run-record directory
exists, as well as when calibration state exists, and directs recovery toward
preserving evidence and selecting a separate state root. Four executable shell
tests cover existing state, receipt-only setup, an unrecorded pipeline, and
resume without a checkpoint; they verify no container is launched and files
are preserved. Fast shell/contract checks now also run on main-branch pushes,
without building or promoting an image. The first hosted
[handoff check](https://github.com/ncsizemore/jheem-containers/actions/runs/36885991550)
passed.

Next:

1. Have another team member launch, interrupt, resume, and locate outputs from
   the runbook. Run one representative full stage with the corrected image to
   measure its production-size memory and output sizes. The earlier cross-server
   timings establish feasibility, not a controlled speed or equivalence result.
2. Complete the stage-3 boundary: either support and verify multiple chains or
   document and test the handoff from isolated container outputs to the native
   workflow. Recorded mode currently refuses multi-chain calibrations. Shared
   writers also require a cross-process locking strategy, beyond the wrapper's
   same-account container check.

The October 1 sequence proposed a sampler correction before same-seed trace
comparisons. The [October 3 plan](#repeatability-plan) refines that order: measure
repeatability through the current seeded workflow first, while keeping the
explicit seed-argument defect and any correction separate. Successful checkpoint
continuation alone remains insufficient evidence of trace equality.

## Separate source from the runtime (2026-10-01) {#separate-source}

The wrapper now preserves analysis code separately from the retained image
([containers `b1a40dc`](https://github.com/ncsizemore/jheem-containers/commit/b1a40dc072dc0cf3983f74b36fa9b683b6fe19b8),
[D-023](../decisions.qmd#d-023)). First use of a calibration code captures a clean
committed checkout; all its locations in that run root share the selection.
A pipeline selects its stages together. New codes can use newer source without
an image build, while subsequent stages and continuations retain their original
source, image ID, manager releases, and seed. The
[operator guide](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/5e441ea6fd58368cce5f2558de29a6b212930649/applications/SHIELD/CONTAINER-PILOT.md)
describes this without requiring a container-repository checkout.

The saved archive and per-file hashes live under `run_sources/`, beside records
and outputs. Both container paths to the snapshot are read-only. The wrapper
verifies saved content before reuse and checks specification/registry startup
against installed packages before detached sampling. Dirty source, incompatible
stage selections, missing snapshots, and explicit changes to saved inputs are
refused. Whole-repository snapshots currently occupy about 580 MiB including
archive and materialized files; NAS capture adds startup I/O. CIFS mount-wide
permissions are supported without relying on per-file `chmod`.

Twenty-eight fast checks cover the helper, wrapper mounts and startup refusal,
source drift, integrity failures, and existing-state preservation; the
[hosted check](https://github.com/ncsizemore/jheem-containers/actions/runs/36921240029)
passed. On shield2,
two new tiny calibration definitions absent from the retained image completed
summary, assembly, and preceding-stage lineage with NAS state. Changing the
original test checkout while the pipeline ran did not change either stage's
saved source. This used an isolated committed fixture based on `06505412`, not
the latest scientific model. Repeating the pipeline verified both stages' output
files and skipped completed work. The
[test definitions](https://github.com/ncsizemore/jheem-containers/blob/b1a40dc072dc0cf3983f74b36fa9b683b6fe19b8/workloads/shield/tests/snapshot_calibration.R)
and [technical reference](https://github.com/ncsizemore/jheem-containers/blob/b1a40dc072dc0cf3983f74b36fa9b683b6fe19b8/workloads/shield/SOURCE-SNAPSHOTS.md)
are in the owning repository.

The current-source trial at analyses `03e3eea5` stopped before MCMC: the registry
refers to `calib.9.23.stage2` before registering it
([early reference](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/03e3eea538d862e84dfd22b3300d56c7ecf11d4c/applications/SHIELD/shield_calib_register.R#L83),
[later definition](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/03e3eea538d862e84dfd22b3300d56c7ecf11d4c/applications/SHIELD/shield_calib_register.R#L153)).
The same startup failure occurred with a direct mount of the clean checkout,
without the snapshot helper, against the retained engine. The container work
does not change that registration. A current-source operator
trial needs a working selection agreed with the model owners. Ordinary SHIELD
also now selects promoted syphilis data by default
([`03e3eea5`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/commit/03e3eea538d862e84dfd22b3300d56c7ecf11d4c));
the recorded pilot retains its explicit manager selection. New source does not
implicitly update those inputs.

These results exercise different source selections. The September 30 full
`calib.9.28.stage0` run predates the registry change introduced in
[`0591d626`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/commit/0591d626ebfde257f81cc60785bfcacd0c44a1e8).
The retained image's successful hosted canary uses `06505412`; the later NAS
source-preservation test deliberately uses a fixture based on that same earlier
source. Neither establishes that the latest calibration definitions can start.
Both the ordinary modular launcher and the recorded startup check source the
whole registry, so an out-of-order definition can stop startup even when that
older calibration was not requested.

A native `calib.10.1.stage0` run was separately observed progressing beyond
4,000 iterations on October 1. A read-only server audit at 23:34 UTC explains
the registration difference: its checkout is at `03e3eea5` with an uncommitted
deletion of exactly the ten-line early duplicate. Removing those lines from the
published file produces the audited working file's SHA-256 exactly. Its modification
time precedes the R process start by about seven seconds. The inspected launcher,
source bootstrap, specification, and likelihood files match their committed
versions. This is a working-source difference, not evidence that the container
introduced a new registration rule. The audit describes files at inspection;
it is not a contemporaneous source receipt from the native launch.

The native log and audited engine identify jheem2 `9578726b`. The
[published engine comparison](https://github.com/CIPHER-Epi/jheem2/compare/ccb1f9bfe40844143dbcec65ffd27829aa39d7ef...9578726b012a2ee380b380ef0203733d1bd81163)
changes only spline functional forms; the audited registration implementation
and source-mode bootstrap match that commit. Those newer spline fixes still
require runtime alignment before reproducing the current calibration. The audit
also identified a [legacy manager fallback](manager-compatibility.qmd#observed-legacy-fallback)
to an older released artifact. Recording the existing source correction and
agreeing on engine and manager selections precede a current-source container
trial; no scientific source or running calibration was changed by the audit.

The shared installation and two intended accounts passed administrator checks:
image loading, persistent user services, shared-input readability, and container
NAS writes. This is not yet an independent operator's calibration exercise.
The installed wrapper also verified and skipped both completed NAS test stages.
Startup locks serialize launches but do not provide
general lifetime or cross-account writer coordination. Multi-chain stage 3,
native handoff, corrected-image full-stage measurement, deterministic replay,
and automatic archival of source/records/results remain open.

## Current-source comparison candidate (2026-10-02) {#current-source-comparison}

The audited registry correction is now recorded on a
[candidate analyses branch](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/commit/041498235821ad7bf0a743be9035a44f2c740f4b).
It removes only the premature duplicate, producing the audited registry bytes
exactly; no remaining calibration definition or likelihood formula changes.
The candidate runtime selects jheem2 `9578726b`, and its optional
`native-2026-10-01` test-input profile identifies the May 5 syphilis artifact,
August 26 census artifact, and seed 0. The retained installed image and its
defaults are unchanged. This selection reproduces the identified native inputs
for comparison, not a recommendation about which data should be used in future
calibrations.

Validation separates three questions:

1. **Execution and preservation:** can the current model start, checkpoint,
   resume, assemble simsets, and retain verified input/output and stage-lineage
   records?
2. **Readable numerical contents:** do completed simsets contain the expected
   stage and location, finite parameter values, and finite population, incidence,
   and diagnosis totals for selected years? The candidate
   [inspector](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/eab6beb0a3131607b978b8f42bc1c87b9592c1a2/applications/SHIELD/R/shield_output_checks.R)
   reports actual values and descriptive ranges. Its initial outcome view sums
   across demographic strata; it is not a stratified equivalence test.
3. **Native/container numerical comparison — planned:** hold source, manager
   bytes, initial conditions, solver settings, and saved parameter values
   constant, then compare trajectories and individual likelihood contributions.
   Relevant stratified outputs belong in this comparison because agreement in
   aggregate totals can hide different subgroup results. Report absolute and
   relative differences and establish justified numerical tolerances before
   treating the result as an acceptance gate.

The first two levels passed in
[hosted run 37000162439](https://github.com/ncsizemore/jheem-containers/actions/runs/37000162439),
using container source `9d0869d4`, analyses `eab6beb0`, engine `9578726b`, and the
native-input profile above. Each Baltimore canary stage produced two simulations
with 173 finite stored parameters. Population, incidence, total diagnoses, and
primary/secondary diagnoses were finite, with no negative totals, for 2010,
2015, 2020, 2025, and 2030. Only two transmission parameters vary in the canary;
the second stage exercises predecessor reuse, not the full scientific stage-1
calibration. Missing/modified simsets and changed-input reuse were rejected.
Both downloaded numerical reports parse as JSON without modifying the files.
The tested image was exported as a time-limited Actions artifact; it has not
replaced the retained release or installed image.

**Later October 2 update:** ordinary SHIELD now selects September 9 and includes
the same registry correction in
[`38b20dcf`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/commit/38b20dcfa1e879c46e5489b0a52ffa1045e91582).
An [operator-reported stage-1 failure](manager-compatibility.qmd#stage1-fallback)
also confirms the practical consequence of loading an unintended older manager.
The May-input canary remains evidence about that historical configuration,
not the baseline for the intended next calibration. First reconcile the
candidate with current master, verify September's manager against the actual
stage-1 likelihood setup, and then use that selection for prospective
native/container comparisons. The passed two-stage canary did not exercise
the scientific stage-1 likelihood.

The shared [loader hardening and identity logging](manager-compatibility.qmd#loader-hardening)
subsequently landed on analyses master at `336df26d`, without deploying a new
image or changing server checkouts. The broader candidate's numerical-output
inspection remains separate from that landing.

Full calibration comparisons follow those fixed-parameter checks and examine
parameter and outcome distributions and sampling diagnostics. The two-iteration
CI canary does not establish convergence. The bounded replay tests below compare
matched same-seed traces separately; they do not require different-seed
calibrations or serialized simset files to be identical. Whether a newer manager
changes scientific conclusions remains a separate question.

## Repeatability validation plan (2026-10-03) {#repeatability-plan}

**Verified evidence:** the initial assessment used analyses `4264842c`, engine
`9578726b`, and sampler `4e0d13e`. The diagnostics later landed as recorded above.
A toy cache check rerun on October 3 reproduced
the ignored explicit seed argument: keeping `seed = 123` but changing prior R
state from `set.seed(1)` to `set.seed(2)` changes stored chunk seeds; keeping
`set.seed(1)` but changing the argument to `456` does not. The
[public constructor](https://github.com/tfojo1/bayesian.simulations/blob/4e0d13e85857396bb0e6e2ac1d244775b2145f75/R/run_interface.R#L181-L217)
does not forward the argument, and the
[chunk-seed generator](https://github.com/tfojo1/bayesian.simulations/blob/4e0d13e85857396bb0e6e2ac1d244775b2145f75/R/cache.R#L235-L261)
uses ambient random state. This check does not run a scientific calibration.

**Workflow hypothesis:** ordinary SHIELD calls `set.seed(0)` before setup, while
recorded mode uses its configured seed at the
[same point](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/4264842ce3fda9fbbc9c3e6717f958c11b5152ca/applications/SHIELD/shield_calib_setup_and_run.R#L64-L114).
An otherwise identical setup could therefore recreate the same chunk schedule
and trace despite the API defect. The [subsequent experiment](#seed-replay-result)
demonstrated fresh-run equality on a bounded fixture, but not equality across
restarts. Any package correction remains separate from characterization of
this workflow ([D-024](../decisions.qmd#d-024)).

**Validation matrix:**

| Comparison | Question and evidence |
|---|---|
| Fixed parameter vectors, native versus container | The [October 3 result](#engine-loading-comparison) compares hand-sourced and installed-package engines within macOS and Linux, and Mac hand-sourced versus Linux container execution. It covers three vectors at one location, not a team server's native environment or full calibration. |
| Two fresh container processes with separate empty output roots | [Passed on the eight-iteration fixture](#seed-replay-result): identical initial parameters, stored chunk seeds, samples, likelihoods, and adaptive state. A changed-seed control changed both the seed schedule and sampled values. |
| Uninterrupted versus interrupted/resumed execution | [Diverged on the same fixture](#seed-replay-result): matched initial/checkpoint state and seeds, but a different accepted proposal by iteration 4. Both resumptions completed and preserved earlier chunks. |
| Matched native versus container calibration | After fixed-parameter checks, assess trace agreement with the actual native source-loading path and container package-loading path explicitly recorded. A mismatch requires locating the first divergence, not immediately blaming the sampler. |

Hold source and manager bytes, initial conditions, solver settings, chain setup,
iteration count, burn-in, thinning, and checkpoint frequency constant. Record
R/package versions, loading mode, RNG settings, and runtime identity. Compare
scientific values rather than whole serialized files containing timestamps or
runtime metadata. Exact same-environment trace equality and justified numerical
tolerances across environments are different acceptance claims; a bounded pass
is not proof of convergence or every multi-chain configuration.

**Compatibility checkpoint:** on October 3, the actual registered stage-1
likelihood passed a local Baltimore check with September's intended manager:
12 finite components at three fixed parameter vectors. May's manager reproduced
the missing-outcome failure during likelihood construction. This check used the
recorded source-loading path, not a native/container comparison, and did not
exercise predecessor output reuse or MCMC. See the
[identities, results, and limits](manager-compatibility.qmd#stage1-check).

The reconciled diagnostics retain production scientific and loader behavior
from analyses `4264842c`. Preserve selections across the
[whole staged run](reproducibility.qmd#run-preservation), then use the replay
counterexample to assess a separately reviewed checkpoint/RNG correction.
Native-server comparison, a representative full stage, and operator handoff
remain separate acceptance steps. Existing native runs can contribute evidence only
to the extent that their loaded inputs and environment are identifiable; do not
alter them or invent missing launch records to construct a comparison.

The deliverable is a short comparison report stating what matched, what differed,
and what was not tested, backed by repeatable scripts in the owning repositories.
Later model derivation follows the separate
[parent-artifact lineage requirement](reproducibility.qmd#derived-lineage);
generalized transmutation is not a prerequisite for these tests.

### Engine-loading comparison (2026-10-03) {#engine-loading-comparison}

Two fresh macOS/R 4.4.2 processes evaluated the real Baltimore stage-1 likelihood
with identical September syphilis and August census manager bytes. One used
`jheem2@9578726b` installed from source into an isolated library; the other used
that revision's existing `R/tests/source_jheem2_package.R` loader. Both consumed
the same saved parameter doubles. The reconciled
[diagnostic candidate](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/commit/94ba72984737d71ea9ca8ed102a8add58b48e6f2)
is analyses `94ba7298`, with scientific source unchanged from master `4264842c`.

| Compared values across three parameter vectors | Observed agreement |
|---|---|
| Population, incidence, total diagnoses, and primary/secondary diagnoses: 2010–2030 annually, retaining 11 ages × 3 races × 3 sex groups (24,948 values) | Exact at full double precision |
| Twelve stage-1 likelihood components per vector (36 values), plus three totals | Exact at full double precision |

The hand-sourced side used a disposable analyses copy with one diagnostic
bootstrap substitution: the recorded `pkgload::load_all()` call invoked the
existing engine source script instead. All other tracked SHIELD/commoncode
file hashes matched. This keeps manager selection offline and isolated while
exercising the different engine-loading mechanism; it is not a new production
loading option or a test of the ordinary native bootstrap in full. The comparator
retains 17-significant-digit values and rejects mismatched source, input, or
parameter identities. Its tests include detecting a one-ULP difference.

The paired Linux check also completed in
[hosted run 37153878619](https://github.com/ncsizemore/jheem-containers/actions/runs/37153878619),
using container source `eff598ab` and image
`sha256:2819cc3ec51ff7ffaf8804ec82212bcc2fe6248ff02748feb76711830ba924a2`.
It used two fresh processes in one Ubuntu 24.04.1/R 4.4.2 image, read-only
source/manager mounts, and no network. Both loading modes agreed exactly on
the same 24,948 outcome values, 36 components, and three totals. The downloaded
reports, not only workflow status, were checked.

The full workflow also passed checkpoint/resume, two-stage summary/assembly,
numerical output inspection, and missing/modified-output and changed-seed
rejection. Each tiny canary stage produced two simulations with 173 finite
parameters and finite selected outcome totals. This is operational continuation
and integrity evidence: the canary's second stage still uses the stage-0
likelihood, and uninterrupted-versus-resumed trace equality was not compared.

The Linux parameter fixture's digest matched the Mac fixture byte-for-byte,
allowing an additional cross-platform comparison: Linux installed-package
versus Mac hand-sourced execution, with matched scientific sources and manager
bytes. Values were not identical across platforms:

| Quantity | Largest absolute difference | Largest relative difference |
|---|---:|---:|
| Population cell | $1.89\times10^{-8}$ | $1.57\times10^{-13}$ |
| Incidence cell | $1.88\times10^{-10}$ | $6.57\times10^{-13}$ |
| Total-diagnosis cell | $2.03\times10^{-10}$ | $1.28\times10^{-12}$ |
| Primary/secondary-diagnosis cell | $1.33\times10^{-10}$ | $2.31\times10^{-12}$ |
| Likelihood component | $4.34\times10^{-10}$ | $1.34\times10^{-13}$ |
| Total log likelihood | $1.64\times10^{-9}$ | $4.65\times10^{-14}$ |

Relative differences divide by the larger absolute value in each pair; the
absolute and relative maxima need not occur in the same cell. For scale, the
largest population difference occurred at values near 120,557. The environments
also differ in BLAS and compiler/platform details; the specific cause of each
numerical difference was not isolated. These measurements are not an adopted
scientific tolerance or proof that MCMC traces will remain identical.

**Limits:** no full native bootstrap, active server run, predecessor reuse,
convergence, or replay claim follows from this fixed-parameter result. The
diagnostics subsequently landed on the default branches on October 3 as
recorded above. The retained image, releases, server checkouts, and active runs
are unchanged. This hosted run does not export an image for installation.

### Seed and checkpoint replay result (2026-10-03) {#seed-replay-result}

The [hosted replay experiment](https://github.com/ncsizemore/jheem-containers/actions/runs/37161484559)
completed four isolated calibrations using the real Baltimore stage-0 model and
likelihood. Each sampled two transmission rates for eight iterations, with
one chain, no burn-in, no thinning, and four two-iteration checkpoints. The
same image, source, offline manager bytes, and single-threaded BLAS setting
were used throughout. The resumed run was interrupted after checkpoints one
and two, with complete cache state verified while paused. Earlier chunk hashes
were unchanged after interruption and after completion.

| Comparison | Observed result |
|---|---|
| Two fresh runs, configured seed 0 | Exact agreement at full double precision: 173 original model parameters, two initial sampled parameters, chunk seeds, all samples and likelihood/prior values, acceptance counts, and adaptive state. |
| Changed-seed control, configured seed 1 | Different chunk seeds and sampled values; the configured seed affects this workflow. |
| Uninterrupted versus twice-resumed, configured seed 0 | The initial values, chunk seeds, and first checkpoint state match. The first stored sample difference is iteration 4, after the first restart. Both resumptions completed successfully. |

At iteration 4, the uninterrupted run retained transmission rates `1.6, 1.6`;
the resumed run accepted `1.5435453720102092, 1.4921837799750717`. Their log
likelihoods were `-16484.35126810809` and `-16475.77615942093`, an absolute
difference of about 8.575. This is a different accepted proposal, not the small
cross-platform rounding differences measured above. The comparison correctly
failed the optional workflow; the existing operational canaries and focused
tests passed. The downloaded reports independently reproduce that result.

**Localized mechanism:** the sampler
[retains its current simulation between chunks in one process](https://github.com/tfojo1/bayesian.simulations/blob/4e0d13e85857396bb0e6e2ac1d244775b2145f75/R/cache.R#L350-L413),
but starts a resumed process without it. It then
[rebuilds the starting simulation after setting the chunk seed](https://github.com/tfojo1/bayesian.simulations/blob/4e0d13e85857396bb0e6e2ac1d244775b2145f75/R/adaptive_blockwise_metropolis.R#L296-L348),
before drawing proposals. In the tested engine,
[simulation metadata seed selection](https://github.com/CIPHER-Epi/jheem2/blob/9578726b012a2ee380b380ef0203733d1bd81163/R/JHEEM_simulation.R#L1620-L1624)
reads `calibrated.parameters`, whereas the kernel exposes
[`calibrated.parameter.names`](https://github.com/CIPHER-Epi/jheem2/blob/9578726b012a2ee380b380ef0203733d1bd81163/R/JHEEM_kernel.R#L567-L573).
A local instrumented check of three real SHIELD fixed-parameter simulations
observed each constructor advancing R's RNG by its metadata seed draw.

The owning repository's
[sampler-only reproducer and concise report](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/bb93142ecc069e4094e3b130c23109babfb98730/applications/SHIELD/tests/REPLAY-COMPARISON.md)
isolate this mechanism: adding one random draw to a deterministic toy simulation
breaks uninterrupted/resumed equality, while preserving RNG state around only
its extra starting call restores equality. This is evidence for an extra
RNG-consuming warm-start call, not a general solution for stochastic simulations.
Changing engine metadata seeding or sampler continuation requires an
owner-reviewed proposal and regression checks; neither package was patched.
Repairing the separate explicit seed argument alone would not address this path.

**Tested identities:** analyses `cd53da8e`, container source `221ab6f8`, engine
`9578726b`, sampler `4e0d13e`, R 4.4.2/Linux x86-64/OpenBLAS, and image
`sha256:c2101eb594e4160a83c6f7113ba16fdb7690ea69be7428e2e5f98f1c1d5b3648`.
Inputs were `syphilis-manager-v2026.09.09` (SHA-256
`c3e3c983d6b4e9c961f735f9c59d45483bd63cfa715cf75c1fae874da2d129e6`)
and `data-managers-v2026.08.26` census (SHA-256
`f8c710684ccfdfb3a5c8e6f4b54caf0417ab67afb82b89ab3259c4b8151e1053`).
Full refs and rerun instructions are in the report. CI's JSON/log artifacts
expire after 14 days; preserve evidence separately when needed beyond that period.

**Limits and next step:** this establishes a bounded fresh-run pass and a
counterexample to identical traces across restarts. It does not assess
convergence, full stages, multiple chains, cross-server equality, or the
scientific validity of an existing calibration. Operational resumption remains
usable within its documented limits. Prepare a focused checkpoint/RNG proposal
for package-owner review before claiming restart-invariant replay. The
diagnostics and report are on the default branches; installed images, active
calibrations, and server checkouts are unchanged.

## Open questions and destination

- Which realistic stage and location should follow the canary, and what
  runtime and memory difference from the ordinary launcher is acceptable?
- Which current model checks can become a reliable must-pass operational
  subset, and which assertions require scientific review?
- After same-image equality is tested, which scientific outputs and tolerances
  define equivalence across materially different numerical platforms?
- What scientific behavior is intended for the future-growth penalty when its
  baseline is zero or near zero?

The runtime adapter, container build, tests, and server runbook belong in
`jheem_analyses` and `jheem-containers`. This page remains the cross-repository
investigation until a retained server pilot uses a current pinned image and the
owning repositories document its supported path; then it can be reduced to
the durable contract and result.
